market_context: Friday midday: the Nasdaq is down about 1.7% and SPY is down 0.7%, while DIA is flat. Chip and AI stocks are weak after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday. October PPI was a bit cooler than expected at +0.3% m/m but still 6.5% y/y. The 10-year yield is about 5.1%, a December Fed hike is fully priced in, and bitcoin fell below $70k for the first time since August.

predictions.reasoning: Bitcoin is on track for a sixth straight weekly decline. Spot ETF outflows, leveraged-long unwinds and Fed hike expectations all point down, and the break below $70k could trigger more liquidations. The MSCI decision to drop Strategy from indexes adds more pressure.

QQQ is already down 1.7% and sits near the low of its day range ($671.71-$688.75), while DIA is flat, so the damage is concentrated in Nvidia and chips. Some dip-buying and short covering into the close is plausible, but the 5.1% yield and rate-hike fears limit the bounce.

SPY is down 0.74% and trading in the lower half of its range. Cooler-than-expected PPI (+0.3% vs +0.4% expected) and a weekly gain still intact favor a modest recovery, though VIX is rising and tech weakness persists.
